jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Teacher Qualified Staff at Temple Beth Israel Eugene
jobs.description: Employer: Temple Beth Israel Eugene Expires: 11/05/2026 The Teacher Qualified Staff will support the general program, and supervise children as a Teacher Qualified staff member as needed for employee breaks, and as a substitute in the event a teacher is absent short term. A Teacher must be at least 18 years of age and meet the qualifications of the position listed in Table 2 of rule 414-300-0100 from the Rules for Certified Child Care Centers of Oregon Department of Education/ Early Learning Division. This position is expected to work no more than 40 hours per week and as a part time employee is not eligible for TBI Preschool’s employer benefits. The Teacher Qualified Program Support Staff will be paid $21 per hour.The ages of children attending TBI Preschool are 30 months- 5 years old with varying developmental abilities. Teacher Qualified Support Staff will receive direction from the Preschool Director, the Rabbi, and other Teacher Qualified staff. This position is primarily responsible for;Record keeping.Supervising children ages 2.5-5 years.Maintaining appropriate teacher to child ratios.Organizing and implementing curriculum.Keeping the classroom orderly and clean.Washing and sanitizing all preparation and eating areas before and after eating and washing/drying/putting away all dishes after use.Providing teaching staff with necessary breaks when needed, and occasionally subbing for staff absences.Other tasks as assignedWhile supervising children, the Teacher Qualified Program Support Staff must keep the required state ratio according to age group and Table 3B as explained in The Office of Childcare’s rules and regulations and may be alone while supervising children. The Teacher qualified Program Support Staff will successfully supervise the activities of all children assigned to the group while in the classroom. With the guidance and direction of the Preschool Director and other Teacher qualified staff members, this position must assist with maintaining accurate record keeping specific to child and staff sign in/outs, staff file, accident/incident reports, training hours, emergency contacts, administration of medication, child observations, and documentation. In accordance with TBI’s Mission, the primary work of the Preschool is to provide a high quality Jewish early childhood education to TBI Members and the broader Lane County Community. A commitment to providing safe, warm, and high-quality care where discovery and growth are fostered through play and creativity. All employees of TBI Preschool will value the uniqueness of each child and nurture their development cognitively, emotionally, socially, ethically, and physically. TBI Preschool celebrates Jewish holidays, Jewish ethics, and fosters a celebration of Jewish identity in a way that is inclusive and respectful to all.The Teacher Qualified Program Support will collaborate with the Preschool Director, Rabbi and Teaching Staff to maintain the following:A 5-Star rating from the Oregon Spark Program.A Reggio inspired environment and philosophy.A low student-to-teacher ratio.Joyfully offer Jewish experiences, and welcome children and families from all cultural and religious backgrounds.A strong reputation among young families, both within the Membership and community.A commitment to personal, ethical and professional growth.A commitment to implement an anti-racist and anti-bias curriculum and environment which is inclusive for all.NAEYC’s Code of Conduct, NAEYC’s position on providing Equitable and Inclusive Early Childhood Education, and Developmentally Appropriate Practice.All TBI Preschool staff are expected to encourage children’s growth in the following areas; Self-esteem and confidence, social emotional development, fine and gross motor coordination, sensory integration, cognitive and adaptive skills, language development and ethical growth and development.Mandatory Requirements and Safety Trainings of the position include:Current enrollment and good standing in the Oregon Criminal History Registry (prior to start of employment)Introduction to Child Care Health and Safety online course (within 30 days of employment)Current Oregon Food Handler’s Card (within 30 days of employment)Current Pediatric First Aid/CPR Certification (within 90 days of employment)Oregon’s Recognizing and Reporting Child Abuse and Neglect online course (within 90 days of employment)Oregon’s Prevention is Better than Treatment online courseOregon’s Foundations of Learning courseMaintain a minimum of 20 hours of continuing education per licensing year, and any training recommendations the Preschool Director or Rabbi Educator assign related to job performance.Please send a resume and cover letter to andyn@tbieugene.org

jobs.title: Per Diem Therapist at Seneca Family of Agencies
jobs.description: Employer: Seneca Family of Agencies Expires: 11/05/2026 Looking for a flexible therapy role where you can make a difference? Join our PHP team as a Per Diem Therapist and provide short-term, intensive mental health services that help clients achieve stability and move forward in their recovery. This position offers the opportunity to facilitate impactful group therapy sessions, collaborate with experienced clinicians, and contribute to a supportive, client-centered environment. This role requires you to be on call for at least 2 of these 3 STEP facility locations: Concord, Fairfield and Petaluma About the STEP ProgramThe STEP (Skills, Transitions, Exploration, and Progress) program provides Partial Hospitalization services to youth ages 12-17. The goal of the STEP program is to provide intensive, short-term stabilization services to enable our clients to step down to lower levels of outpatient mental health treatment. All groups are designed to teach youth the skills necessary to help them learn about their mental health, provide psychoeducation, and help them learn skills to feel better and be safe. STEP consists of a multidisciplinary team of counselors, clinicians, a nurse, psychiatrist, and program supervisor. About Seneca Seneca Family of Agencies has been nominated among the Bay Area’s Top Workplaces for several consecutive years. We’re committed to providing traditionally marginalized communities with a network of excellent mental health, community-based, and educational services. We are committed to building a diverse staff and our programs deeply engage in conversations and training on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion to bring equity and justice to the youth and families we serve. Responsibilities:Hold clinical integrity for programMaintain on-time clinical documentationFacilitate group, individual, and family therapyFacilitate risk assessments, case management, and discharge planningProvide appropriate clinical trainings and information to staff when neededDevelop and maintain relationships with community members and providersProactively problem solving when identified issues ariseAssist with intakes, as neededSupport other Seneca programs when client enrollment permitsUtilize crisis communication and de-escalation techniques as per Seneca's crisis response trainingQualifications:Master’s degree in psychology, counseling, social work, or related subject areaRegistered with California BBS: ACSW, AMFT, APCC, or fully licensedRequired to be on call for at least 2 of these 3 STEP facility locations: Concord, Fairfield and Petaluma Seneca also additional locations in Oakland, San Jose and Salinas with available per diem shifts At least 21 years of ageTB test clearance, fingerprinting clearance, and any other state/federal licensing or certification requirementsValid driver's license, clean driving record, and consistent access to a personal vehicleSchedulePer diem, on-site at one of Seneca's 6 STEP locations: Oakland, Concord, Fairfield, Petaluma, San Jose, and SalinasMonday - Friday, 8am - 4pm BenefitsStarting at $36.25 - $38.75 per hourActual salary is dependent on creditable experience above the minimum qualifications for the roleSalary increases each yearAdditional compensation provided upon passing bilingual language proficiency examAbundant promotional opportunities across the agencySeneca supports clinicians towards licensure and beyond: We provide individual and group supervision, regular clinical case conferences, and licensure and renewal courses led by field experts

jobs.title: Behavioral Instructor at Inspira Behavior
jobs.description: Employer: Inspira Behavior Expires: 11/05/2026 Job OverviewWe are seeking a dedicated and compassionate Behavior Therapist to join our multidisciplinary mental health and behavioral services team. The ideal candidate will possess a strong foundation in behavioral health interventions, with a focus on supporting individuals with developmental disabilities, autism spectrum disorder, and other mental health conditions. As a Behavior Therapist, you will deliver evidence-based therapies, conduct patient assessments, and collaborate with families and healthcare professionals to promote positive behavioral change. This role offers an opportunity to make a meaningful difference in clients' lives through personalized care and innovative therapeutic techniques.Duties· Implement behavioral therapy programs utilizing applied behavior analysis (ABA) and other evidence-based practices tailored to individual needs.· Conduct comprehensive patient assessments, including intake evaluations and diagnostic evaluations using ICD-9 and ICD-10 coding systems.· Develop and modify treatment plans based on ongoing data collection, progress monitoring, and clinical research findings.· Provide direct support and counseling to children, adolescents, and adults with developmental disabilities, PTSD, or other mental health challenges.· Facilitate individual and group therapy sessions incorporating modalities such as psychodynamic therapy, art therapy, dance therapy, or cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT).· Collaborate with families, caregivers, and educational teams to implement behavior management strategies within home or school settings.· Maintain accurate medical documentation and ensure compliance with HIPAA regulations to protect patient confidentiality.· Manage crisis situations effectively through crisis intervention techniques and crisis management protocols.Skills· Extensive knowledge of psychotherapy modalities including cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), psychodynamic therapy, and behavior management strategies.· Proficiency in motivational interviewing techniques to foster client engagement and motivation for change.· Experience working with children, individuals with autism spectrum disorder, disabilities, or in pediatric settings; familiarity with special education is advantageous.· Strong background in medical terminology, ICD coding (ICD-9/ICD-10), medical records management, and clinical research methodologies.· Ability to perform patient assessments, diagnostic evaluations, and case management effectively within outpatient or inpatient environments.· Skilled in crisis intervention, crisis management, addiction counseling, grief counseling, chronic pain counseling, and PTSD care.· Familiarity with telehealth platforms for remote service delivery; experience in outpatient clinics or hospital settings is preferred.· Competence in data collection for research purposes and experience with CPT coding for billing purposes.· Excellent communication skills combined with a compassionate approach to patient care; ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams focused on behavioral health outcomes. Join us in delivering impactful behavioral health services that empower individuals to achieve their full potential through compassionate care and innovative therapeutic practices! Pay: $22.00 - $29.00 per hourEducation Requirements:***HS level is okay, BA preferred, minimal afternoon hours at first with opportunity to grow***** Work Location: In person

jobs.description: Employer: JVS SoCal Expires: 11/05/2026 Program Instructor - BankWork$®COMPANY: JVS SoCalPOSITION: Program Instructor - BankWork$®LOCATION: Los Angeles, CASALARY: $29.00 - $32.00 per hour + benefitsLINK TO APPLY: https://phx.us-west.paycomonline.net/v4/ats/web.php/portal/BF9B0592862A911E3FF9FDB92A09A03B/jobs/21074 DESCRIPTIONThe BankWork$® Instructor’s primary responsibility is to provide coaching and training sessions to participants of the BankWork$® program utilizing existing curriculum and training materials as well as developing additional curriculum in soft skills, business acumen, and job search techniques to support the transition of participants to full employment. Secondary responsibilities include working with team members at the Institute for Career Opportunity (ICO) to recruit, evaluate and screen candidates for enrollment and to provide business outreach to all area banks to develop job opportunities for graduates by cultivating and maintaining relationships with bank recruiters and managers. entrepreneurial spirit, and attention to detailAbility to perform comfortably in a business and social service environmentStrong written and oral communication/presentation skillsDuties and responsibilities are carried out with considerable independence within the framework of established policies, procedures and guidelinesMust have reliable transportation for conveyance to locations around greater Los Angeles KEY RESPONSIBILITIESUse provided curriculum materials to deliver retail bank training classes responsive to the needs of the banking industry.Provide individual and group job preparation to develop the habits and attitudes needed to be successful in the workplaceCoach clients in developing job skills, resumes, cover letters etc. and provide clients with job search information including assistance completing on-line job applications Closely coordinate with Director to maximize participant placement in employment in banking positionsInterview candidates for enrollment and administer testing to determine eligibilityMaintain accurate documentation on classroom performance and participation for each student enrolled in the program.Delivers instruction at other locations as needed.Show demonstrated ability to interact with people of different cultures.Perform related duties as assigned by managementKey Performance Indicators are:Number of participants enrolled in the programsParticipant program completion rateParticipant placement rateParticipant job retention ratePositive employer feedback and overall satisfaction with hiresOutcomes will be achieved by way of:Program Training and SupportCase ManagementPost-Instruction ActivitiesOutreach and RecruitingReporting and Monitoring *** Full details of Key Responsibilities can be provided if requestedPHYSICAL DEMANDSMust be able to operate standard office equipment; will work in business, classroom and other various settings; frequently stands, walks, sits and climbs in performing duties in the office and at offsite locations; required to talk and hear, both in person and by telephone, use computers and standard office equipment; frequently lifts and carries up to 5lbs, occasionally up to 25lbs. ABOUT JVS SOCALFounded in 1931, JVS-SoCal is a nonprofit, non-sectarian social service agency providing job training, education, career services, mentoring, and placement assistance to diverse and multicultural populations, transforming lives and empowering individuals to achieve sustainable employment and financial independence. JVS SoCal currently serves over 30,000 clients annually at over 20 locations throughout Southern California. As JVS SoCal continues to grow, we continue to look for qualified, dedicated staff to join us and play a role in transforming lives and bettering our communities throughout SoCal and beyond!ICO programs provide opportunity to individuals with barriers to employment to embark upon a career in a high growth/high demand business sector. In partnership with Southern California’s top banking institutions, our team prepares job seekers for positions in the financial services industry as a first step on a career ladder that offers extraordinary potential. This intensive eight-week program offers targeted job training, placement support and post-employment coaching. JVS BankWork$® has achieved a solid track record in the placement and retention rates of its graduates. ICO programs all include technical training, case management, job placement support and job retention guidance. JVS SoCal will consider qualified applicants with a criminal history pursuant to the California Fair Chance Act. You do not need to disclose your criminal history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if JVS SoCal is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating or rehabilitative evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background check report. Find out more about the Fair Chance Act by visiting www.calcivilrights.ca.gov/fair-chance-act .

jobs.description: Employer: Bloomingdale Christian Church Expires: 11/06/2026 Please visit our website or look through the information below. https://www.bdalechurch.org/about-7 We’re Hiring: Director of Family Ministries(Online job posting)Location: Rural Bloomingdale / Van Buren County Area, MichiganPosition Type: Full-TimeReports To: Lead PastorAbout UsWe are a growing, non-denominational church of about 220 people with a vibrant heart for the next generation—nearly a quarter of our congregation is made up of kids and teens! We hold firmly to theologically conservative, Christ-centered truths, but we take a modern, tech-forward approach to how we build our programs, communicate with families, and run our ministries.We recently shifted from a traditional committee structure to a dynamic, team-based ministry model. We believe the church’s job isn't to replace parents, but to equip them as the primary disciplers of their kids while creating safe, high-energy environments where young people encounter Jesus and build a sense of belonging in His larger family.The OpportunityWe are looking for a Director of Family Ministries who loves building teams, inspiring volunteers, and helping families thrive.Your primary mission is to serve as a "leader of leaders." While carrying the majority of teaching and ministry execution, we want you to leave plenty of room for others to share their gifting in the “spotlight” as well. It will be important for you to recruit, coach, and shepherd volunteer team leaders who lead our kids and youth week in and week out.Where You’ll Focus Your Energy60% Kids Ministry (Birth – 5th Grade): Cast vision and refine our current nursery, Sunday morning Beginner’s Church, Kidz Link, and Sunday evening Gospel Kids environments. You will ensure gospel-centered curriculum (like The Gospel Project) is taught effectively, keep safety tight, and make sure the "Kids Zone" is a place kids find engaging and meaningful.20% Middle School Ministry: Build a dedicated, relational middle school program from the ground up. As this group grows, you will help lay the runway for expanding into high school ministry over time.20% Assistant Ministerial Duties: Support the wider ministry of the church as a member of the overall leadership team. Specifics would depend on the candidate’s particular skills, interests and qualifications in relation to the needs that arise. Parent Partnership: Build real, approachable relationships with parents. You will serve as a trusted resource, offering practical tools, digital communication, and occasional workshops to help them disciple their kids at home.Team Building & Volunteer Care: Move away from "need-based" appeals ("we need two warm bodies") and recruit through vision. You'll host pre-service huddles, coach team captains, and find creative ways to appreciate and refuel volunteers so everyone feels valued and nobody burns out.Operational Excellence: Use modern tools like Planning Center for check-ins, service planning, and volunteer scheduling to keep things running smooth, safe, and efficient.Who You AreA Team Builder & Coach: You love spotting potential in people, inviting them into ministry, and equipping them to succeed. You also know how to work and play as part of a larger team.Theologically Grounded: You believe the Bible tells one cohesive story pointing to Jesus. You understand and passionately teach the Gospel, not just moralized life lessons.Tech-savvy & Adaptable: You are comfortable using software and technology (or quick to learn) to streamline systems and stay connected with families.At Home in a Rural Setting: You appreciate the warmth, rhythms, and relational nature of ministering in a rural community.Relational & Accessible: Parents and volunteers find you easy to talk to, supportive, and dependable.Capacity over formal education: While we will only require a high school diploma, college or seminary credits or degrees will be appreciated. More than formal education, however, we are looking for one exhibiting leadership capacity and solid character traits; someone who is responsible, diligent, intentional, resourceful, productive, resilient and intelligent.Salary Range:The compensation package for this position will be a salary range from $45k-$60k depending on level of education, prior ministry experience and demonstrated competencies. Additionally, the package includes: Health insurance reimbursement package.Church parsonage housing option.Ready to Apply?If you have a heart for the next generation and equipping others to lead, we’d love to hear from you.Please send your resume and a brief intro telling us about your heart for family ministry to: dstafford@cornerstoneag-llc.com
